chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'The birds — what may be eaten from them?' So he said: 'Do not eat from them what does not have a gizzard.'

key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: Birds — the generic term for all bird species, here used as the subject of a halal/haram inquiry
key_terms.قَانِصَةٌ: Gizzard — the muscular stomach of birds used for grinding food; its presence is a jurisprudential sign of a permissible bird in Shia fiqh

ai.seo_question: Which birds are halal to eat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: The narrator asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) which birds are permissible to eat. The Imam gives a concise jurisprudential criterion: any bird that lacks a gizzard (qanisa) is forbidden to eat. This ruling is part of the broader Shia fiqh tradition distinguishing lawful from unlawful birds, where the gizzard is one of the distinguishing signs of a halal bird along with having a crop (hawsala) and a spur (isba') on its foot.
